chunks: From him, from Ḥusayn ibn Ḥammād ibn ʿUdays, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from al-Qāsim ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Abū al-Khaṭṭāb was mentioned, so he cursed him, then said: “He would not retain anything. I told him that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had the sun set for him in such-and-such a place, and he performed the maghrib prayer at al-Shajarah, while between them were six miles. I informed him of that regarding travel, but he placed it in the context of residence.”

key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence, the state of being settled and not traveling
key_terms.ذُكِرَ: was mentioned or brought up in discussion
key_terms.غَابَتْ: set, referring to the sun’s setting
key_terms.لَعَنَهُ: he invoked a curse upon him
key_terms.يَحْفَظُ: to preserve or accurately retain what was heard

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describe Abū al-Khaṭṭāb’s distortion of a report about the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This report relates that Imam Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام condemned Abū al-Khaṭṭāb for failing to preserve what he had been told accurately. The Imam explains that a report concerning the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during travel was misapplied to residence, highlighting the importance of precise transmission in matters connected to salat and hadith.
